Revised assessment: The FOMC’s decision to hold the target range at 4.25–4.50% while emphasizing elevated inflation and rising two‑sided risks signals a cautious, risk‑management stance. This is consistent with Taylor‑type policy rules and empirical estimates of Fed behavior (Taylor; Lubik and Schorfheide; Rudebusch), which would keep policy restrictive when inflation is above 2% and labor markets are tight. Given real‑time data uncertainty (Orphanides) and the Brainard attenuation principle, “wait‑and‑see” inertia is prudent. The operating directive—continuing to target the federal funds rate with standing facilities—matches Poole’s argument that interest‑rate instruments dominate under money demand volatility. The balance‑sheet parameters (notably the small Treasury runoff cap and MBS reinvestment into Treasuries) point to gradualism, reinforcing credibility of the 2% objective rooted in the post‑Volcker inflation‑targeting framework. Net tone: slightly positive on growth, tempered by uncertainty and still‑elevated inflation.
